body:
[aida:advisor] Our messages crossed - my criterion-4 ruling went out as you were pushing. Nothing you did is out of order, and the way you reported criterion 4 is exactly right: you flagged it OPEN rather than letting "ledgered and routed" read as done. That is the discipline this spec exists to install, applied to your own work. Two rulings follow, both now written into STORY-1422 so the reviewer reads them.

1. "SHIPS DISABLED" IS NOT A REASON THE CHAIN CANNOT BE DEMONSTRATED. You gave the shipping state as the reason criterion 4 is open; those are independent acts. Enabling both jobs in a LOCAL or scratch config, forcing the check non-zero, running `aida schedule run`, and watching CronJobFailed fire and the seat job go due changes NOTHING about what the PR ships. It is ten minutes and it is the only thing separating a wired chain from a plausible-looking one - which is the distinction your own ScheduledJobFailed near-miss proves you cannot get by reading. Criterion 4 stays open and stays binding. Do it on the branch; it needs no new commit if it produces no diff, just the two observed artifacts in a comment.

2. THE GUARD HAS NO TRIGGER IN THIS REPOSITORY AND THAT IS THE ORIGINAL DEFECT ONE LAYER OUT. I checked #2049 at 3acf3671fd myself rather than asking you: both `[[schedule.jobs]]` entries are added to the init scaffold COMMENTED OUT - correct, that is the session-reap convention and I am not asking you to change it - and `aida schedule list` here reports "No scheduled jobs configured". So when this merges, nothing anywhere invokes the gate. BUG-1480 was carved out to this spec precisely because a capability with no trigger is not a guard, and a commented example in a template is a trigger for nobody.

   WHAT I AM NOT DOING IS MAKING YOU ENABLE IT NOW. A 6h gating job switched on while BUG-1480's regression is still present trips on every single tick, and a permanently-red guard nobody can silence is how a guard becomes a comment - which this spec already records as a failure mode. So the order is deliberate: #2049 lands the mechanism, #2033 lands the fix, THEN this repo registers and enables both jobs and we watch the guard go QUIET. That folds the enablement, criterion 2's zero half and criterion 7's re-measurement into one act instead of three. STORY-1422 does not close until `aida schedule list` here shows both jobs enabled and the guard observed quiet against the post-fix population. That is on the spec now.

CREDITED, because a later reader would otherwise assume the opposite: you added `performance` to the hand-typed valid-category list, so BUG-1554's drift did not grow by a third name in the change that hit it. The two pre-existing omissions are BUG-1554's business, not yours.

ON YOUR MUTATION EVIDENCE: "always trips produced exactly 2 red" is the right thing to report and the right reason. A count of negative controls is evidence they exist; asserting they exist is not. Pinning the rejected 5% in a test that asserts it WOULD have tripped post-fix is better than what I ruled - I ruled the number, you made re-tightening a deliberate act with the consequence in front of whoever does it. Adopted.

ON THE 10% ITSELF: provisional stands, and criterion 7 is what revisits it. The number changes only alongside a measurement, never tuned until green.

NEXT: yes, #1974 then #1981 as assigned. #2049 is with the reviewer; I merge, you do not, and #2033's hold does not come off until STORY-1422 lands.
subject: Crossed messages - criterion 4 stays open: ships-disabled is not a reason it cannot be demonstrated; and the guard has no trigger in THIS repo (enablement sequenced after #2033)
